scientificReason.mechanism: For one balanced reaction write gas stoichiometric exponents nu_i positive for products and negative for reactants. With a common temperature and ideal gas partial pressures p_i=c_iRT, multiply p_i**nu_i over gas species: Qp=Qc(RT)**sum(nu_i). At equilibrium this is the conventional dimensional Kp/Kc conversion. Thus the mathematical relation, conversions and assessment of ideal-gas limitations coherently contribute to the current target. The actual derivation operator needs its own assessable witness rather than conversion-by-given-formula alone.
scientificReason.unitsAndStandards: The dimensional textbook quotients acquire pressure or concentration units raised to deltaNuGas. If Kp and Kc instead mean dimensionless quotients built from p_i/p0 and c_i/c0, the factor is (RT*c0/p0)**deltaNuGas. A bare RT factor cannot be combined with arbitrary standard-normalized quotients while claiming all quantities dimensionless. Use matching pressure/concentration units and R, the same reaction direction/normalization and temperature. The thermodynamic activity equilibrium constant is not two unrelated dimensional numbers.
scientificReason.limits: The signed exponent sums only gaseous species. Pure solids/liquids have unit activity under the specified convention and do not contribute to deltaNuGas; dissolved species/nonideal gases cannot blindly be transformed by p=cRT. At appreciable nonideality partial-pressure activities require fugacity coefficients, and concentration activities require their own activity model. No universal pressure threshold or temperature-independent constant is claimed.
